headline: Cloudflare has released Clef, a pair of open AI models that choose between set options instead of writing text, as a rival to the start-up model Jev.
score_reason: Lowered from 5: Cloudflare announced Clef on 1 Oct; the 8 Oct InfoQ piece is a follow-up.
importance_line: Developers building AI agents get a free-to-download alternative to Jev that also reads images, but the benchmark results are Cloudflare's own and commenters questioned whether they prove real-world reliability.
summary: InfoQ reports that Cloudflare released the open-weight Clef models (27 billion and 9 billion parameters; open-weight means the trained settings are published for anyone to download), which return a probability for each allowed answer in a single pass rather than writing text; Cloudflare announced them on 1 Oct 2026, so the 8 Oct piece is a follow-up. Cloudflare says Clef accepts images and longer input than TypeSafe's text-only Jev, and its own tests give the smaller Clef-Flash a median delay of 38.8 milliseconds, while developers on Hacker News and Reddit questioned what the benchmarks prove.
notes: 1 Oct date comes from Cloudflare Blog's listing in Google News results, not from the InfoQ text.
